label: Fire TV Cube (3rd gen) streaming player, 10/100 Ethernet + Wi-Fi 6E
description: Amazon Fire TV Cube (3rd generation, 2022, build model AFTGAZL) — octa-core 4K HDR streaming player with a real RJ45 on the back: 10/100 Mbps Ethernet, alongside Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax tri-band, 2.4/5/6 GHz) and Bluetooth 5.0. Also has HDMI 2.1 input and output (ARC) and one USB 2.0 port, which are not network interfaces. This is the Fire TV a lab can cable.
notes: Ethernet is 10/100, NOT gigabit: Amazon's Fire TV Cube specification lists 'Ethernet: 10/100 Mbps' and repeats '10/100 Ethernet' under Connectors/Ports, so eth0 is a 100BASE-TX port with speedCaps 10/100 and it auto-negotiates down against a 10/100/1000 switch port. Any claim of 1GbE on this model is wrong. Wi-Fi is Wi-Fi 6E ('Wifi 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax; 2x2 MIMO (2.4 GHz, 5.0 GHz and 6GHz Tri-band)'), Bluetooth is 5.0 with BLE. As on the Stick, Amazon publishes no PHY rate, so the 1.2G on wlan0 is the 2x2, 80 MHz 802.11ax client rate used to place the radio in the ax band set. eth0 carries an explicit poeIn: 0 because the engine's PoE-PD heuristic keys on the substring 'cube' (it was written for MikroTik/Ubiquiti Cube CPEs) and would otherwise treat this mains-powered player as an 802.3af powered device. The HDMI 2.1 input/output and the single USB 2.0 port are not modelled: the catalogue does not model USB or HDMI as interfaces. Mains powered, no PoE, so no PoE capability token.
